description: Pointsman is a decision service on Cloudflare Workers. A client system sends a state (a resident's road report, a new issue, a deploy's stack events) to `POST /v1/decide/{profile}`; a language model answers the profile's typed questions; the profile's rules turn the answers into an action (`auto`, `review` or a custom one); every decision is logged with its profile version and model. One Worker per integrator, deployed from a private config repository that holds the profiles. Clients: the FIWARE bridge, the GitHub connector, two GitHub Actions and MCP agents. The state author is the untrusted surface; token holders are trusted for their profiles; the operator is trusted.

trust_boundaries.boundary: `engine-api`: a finding matters if it is reachable from a request that carries a valid token, or from the `state`, `ref` or `callback_url` such a request carries, or from a model backend's response; the internal call (`InternalEngine.decide`) only from a Worker in the same Cloudflare account with a service binding, and only with `INTERNAL_CLIENT` set; since pointsman#221 (`v0.16.0`) also `InternalEngine.get`, `resolve` and `close`, and `POST /v1/reviews/{id}/close`; `/connectors/<id>/` from any request, under the connector's own authentication, its in-process engine only through `/v1/` with its own token, and the queue consumer from the Worker's queue. A finding that needs an invalid or missing token on an HTTP route is a finding against `P-AUTH-REQUIRED` (§1.11).
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: reachable from a request with a valid token, from the state, ref or callback_url it carries, or from a model backend response; the internal call (InternalEngine) only from a Worker in the same Cloudflare account with a binding, and only with INTERNAL_CLIENT set; /connectors/<id>/ from any request, under the connector's own authentication, and the queue consumer from the Worker's queue; since pointsman#221 (v0.16.0) also InternalEngine get, resolve and close, and POST /v1/reviews/{id}/close
trust_boundaries.source: threat-model.md §1.4, maintainer ruling 2026-10; docs/adapters.md "Internal calls"; docs/connectors.md "Where it runs"

trust_boundaries.boundary: `engine-facts`: reachable from the geometry at a profile's `at` path in the client's state, from the pull request (`repo`, `number`, `head`) at a GitHub fact's `at` path, or from a tile, routing, GitHub API or npm registry response, including the workflow files, patches, comments, reviews and statuses those responses carry, the head statuses of other pull requests, and the asking client's own earlier decisions.
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: reachable from the geometry at a profile's `at` path in the client's state, from the pull request (repo, number, head) at a GitHub fact's `at` path, or from a tile, routing, GitHub API or npm registry response, including workflow files, patches, comments, reviews and statuses, other pull requests' head statuses, and the asking client's own earlier decisions
trust_boundaries.source: threat-model.md §1.4; docs/profile-format.md "Facts", "GitHub pull requests", "CodeRabbit reviews"; docs/modules.md "Facts from the decision log"

trust_boundaries.boundary: `engine-callbacks`: reachable from `callback_url` and from the receiver's response.
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: reachable from callback_url or from the receiver's response

trust_boundaries.boundary: `engine-mcp`: reachable from an MCP tool call with a valid API token or OAuth access token, or from the OAuth routes before login (consent page, client registration, GitHub callback).
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: reachable from an MCP tool call with a valid API token or OAuth access token, or from the OAuth routes before login

trust_boundaries.boundary: `bridge`: reachable from a notification that carries the shared secret, from the entity bodies in it, from a queue message, or from a broker or Pointsman response, in its own Worker or under `/connectors/fiware/` inside the engine Worker.
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: reachable from a notification carrying the shared secret, from the entities in it, from a queue message, or from a broker or Pointsman response, in its own Worker or under /connectors/fiware/ inside the engine Worker

trust_boundaries.boundary: `connector-github`: reachable from a webhook that carries a valid `X-Hub-Signature-256` (pull-request, review and check-suite events; `closed` only with the decision comment), from the pull request the connector then reads from GitHub (its title, description and diff, written by the pull-request author), from a GitHub API response including the review decision, or from the engine's answer. Since pointsman#221 and #222 (`v0.16.0`), also from a decision read back from the engine and, where answers are on, from signed `check_run` `requested_action` and (with the command) `issue_comment` `created` webhooks, their sender and the comment's text, and GitHub's answers about the person's permission and the head's newest push. A webhook without a valid signature is a finding against `P-CONNECTOR-WEBHOOK-SIGNED` (§1.11).
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: reachable from a webhook with a valid X-Hub-Signature-256 (pull-request, review and check-suite events; closed only with the decision comment or answers), from the pull request it then reads (title, description, diff by the pull-request author), from a GitHub API response including the review decision, or from the engine's answer; since pointsman#221 (v0.16.0) from a decision read back; since pointsman#222 (v0.16.0), where answers are on, from check_run requested_action and (with the command) issue_comment created webhooks, their sender and the comment's text, and GitHub's answers about the person's permission and the head's newest push
trust_boundaries.source: threat-model.md §1.4; docs/github-connector.md "Safety", "The decision comment", "Asking a person", "Answering in the pull request"

trust_boundaries.boundary: `action-triage`: reachable from the issue title and body in the event payload, or from Pointsman's response.
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: reachable from the issue title and body in the event payload, or from Pointsman's response

trust_boundaries.boundary: `action-deploy-watch`: reachable from CloudFormation stack events or from Pointsman's response. The `run` command and the stack names come from the workflow and are trusted.
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: reachable from CloudFormation stack events or from Pointsman's response; run and stacks are trusted workflow inputs

trust_boundaries.boundary: `config-repo`: reachable from a pull request to the config repository or from the operator's own command line; both are trusted authors (§1.7).
trust_boundaries.reachability_precondition: reachable from a pull request to the config repository or from the operator's command line; both are trusted authors

known_misuse.pattern: acting on a test: true decision as if it were logged
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Acting on a `test: true` decision as if it were logged (`R-IGNORE-TEST-DECISIONS`).
known_misuse.instead: check the test field; keep test tokens out of production clients

known_misuse.pattern: reading p as the model's accuracy and setting thresholds without a margin
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Reading `p` as "the model is 90 % accurate" and setting thresholds without a margin (`D-MODEL-ACCURACY`).
known_misuse.instead: treat p as the model's probability; keep a margin; re-check examples after model updates

known_misuse.pattern: citing the decision log as proof that a report was true or that a named person resolved it
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Citing the decision log as proof that a report was true or that a named person resolved it (`D-LOG-TRUTH`, `D-REVIEWER-IDENTITY`).
known_misuse.instead: treat the log as the engine's record; authenticate people in the client

known_misuse.pattern: one --profiles '*' token shared by every client
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Using one `--profiles '*'` token for every client, so the log cannot tell clients apart and a leak exposes every profile (`R-SCOPED-TOKENS`).
known_misuse.instead: one scoped token per client

known_misuse.pattern: building deploy-watch's run or stacks from issue or pull-request text
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Building deploy-watch's `run` or `stacks` from issue or pull-request text (`R-ACTION-INPUTS`).
known_misuse.instead: set them in the workflow only

known_misuse.pattern: a callback receiver that acts without checking the signature and timestamp, or that is not idempotent
known_misuse.why_unsafe: A callback receiver that acts on the payload without checking the signature and timestamp, or that is not idempotent (`R-VERIFY-CALLBACK`).
known_misuse.instead: verify the HMAC and timestamp; dedupe on decision_id

known_misuse.pattern: a subscription that limits notification.attributes to the inputs so the result attribute never arrives and every notification decides again
known_misuse.why_unsafe: A bridge subscription that limits `notification.attributes` to the inputs, so the result attribute never arrives and every notification decides again (`R-BRIDGE-SUBSCRIPTION`).
known_misuse.instead: leave notification.attributes unset or include the result attribute

known_misuse.pattern: mcp.visible: true on a profile whose questions or decisions are not for every organization member
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Setting `mcp.visible: true` on a profile whose questions or decisions are not for every organization member (`R-MCP-VISIBLE`).
known_misuse.instead: keep such profiles token-only

known_misuse.pattern: putting secrets or identifying free text into ref
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Putting secrets or an identifying free text into `ref` (`R-STATE-IS-DATA`).
known_misuse.instead: use an opaque reference such as an issue URL

known_misuse.pattern: sending personal data in state with the AI Gateway's logs on and no retention decision
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Sending personal data in `state` with the AI Gateway's logs on and no retention decision (`R-DATA-MINIMISATION`).
known_misuse.instead: set collect_logs: false or decide retention first

known_misuse.pattern: making a consequential action the policy's default so a missing fact or a steered answer falls through to it
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Making a consequential action (`publish`, `cancel`) the policy's default action, so a missing fact or a steered answer falls through to it (`R-REVIEW-PATH`).
known_misuse.instead: default to review

known_misuse.pattern: giving the GitHub fact credential write permissions, or a classic token that reaches every repository of its owner
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Giving the GitHub fact credential write permissions, or a classic token that reaches every repository of its owner, so a leaked Worker secret can change repositories (`R-GITHUB-CREDENTIAL`, `R-GITHUB-REPOSITORIES`).
known_misuse.instead: a fine-grained token or GitHub App with read permissions on the repositories the deployment decides about

known_misuse.pattern: an allowing rule that counts on an earlier blocking rule while GitHub facts can be missing, or a glob such as *.md meant to cover every folder
known_misuse.why_unsafe: An allowing rule that counts on an earlier blocking rule while GitHub facts can be missing, or a glob such as `*.md` that was meant to cover every folder (`R-GITHUB-POSITIVE-RULES`).
known_misuse.instead: check missing facts first; write allowing conditions as known positive values; use **/*.md for every folder

known_misuse.pattern: reading github_checks.green as proof that the intended jobs ran when required checks are matched by name only
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Reading `github_checks.green` as proof that the intended jobs ran when the required checks are matched by name only (`D-GITHUB-CHECK-NAMES`, `R-GITHUB-RULES`).
known_misuse.instead: require checks as ruleset workflows or tie them to their app

known_misuse.pattern: using author_sole_code_owner to skip a review while CODEOWNERS itself is not protected on the base branch
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Using `author_sole_code_owner` to skip a review while `CODEOWNERS` itself is not protected on the base branch, so whoever merges a change to it decides who is the only owner (`D-FACT-DATA-AS-PUBLISHED`).
known_misuse.instead: protect CODEOWNERS on the base branch, for example with a code-owner review for changes to it

known_misuse.pattern: acting on a decision for a later push of the same pull request
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Acting on a decision for a later push of the same pull request (`R-GITHUB-ACT-ON-HEAD`).
known_misuse.instead: act only for the head commit the request named; decide again after a push

known_misuse.pattern: mapping approve on a branch whose ruleset does not dismiss stale approvals
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Mapping `approve` on a branch whose ruleset does not dismiss stale approvals, so an approval of an older commit counts after a push until the connector's next run (`R-CONNECTOR-APPROVE`).
known_misuse.instead: turn on dismissal of stale approvals before mapping approve

known_misuse.pattern: mapping approve from a profile whose allowing rule rests on AI answers about the title, description or diff
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Mapping `approve` from a profile whose allowing rule rests on AI answers about the title, description or diff, which the author writes, instead of requiring the facts and using the answers only as extra conditions (`D-APPROVAL-ON-FACTS`, `R-CONNECTOR-APPROVE`).
known_misuse.instead: approve only on facts, with positive rules

known_misuse.pattern: approving a dependency bump on github_bump alone, or with release_age_days 0
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Approving a dependency bump on `github_bump` alone, without `github_pr` saying who made the commits, or on a `release_age_days` of 0 (`R-GITHUB-BUMP-PAIR`).
known_misuse.instead: pair with github_pr and an age margin

known_misuse.pattern: giving the GitHub connector a test token, so it acts on decisions that are not logged
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Giving the GitHub connector a test token: since `v0.13.1` it acts on none of its decisions (each check run says `test decision: nothing done` and its approvals are withdrawn), so the deployment silently does nothing (`P-CONNECTOR-ANSWER-CHECKED`, `R-CONNECTOR-APPS`).
known_misuse.instead: its own normal token limited to its profiles, or the internal call

known_misuse.pattern: one GitHub App for the facts and the connector, so the Worker that sends pull-request text to a model holds a key that can write
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Using one GitHub App for the facts and the connector, so the Worker that sends pull-request text to a model also holds a key that can write (`R-CONNECTOR-APPS`).
known_misuse.instead: two apps: read-only facts app, connector app only in the connector Worker

known_misuse.pattern: INTERNAL_CLIENT with more profiles than the connector uses, or another client's name
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Giving `INTERNAL_CLIENT` more profiles than the connector uses, or the name of another client, so bound Workers decide in that client's history (`R-INTERNAL-CALL`).
known_misuse.instead: only the connector's profiles, under the client name of its token

known_misuse.pattern: counting on a firewall or rate-limit rule on /v1/ to limit the connector after switching to internal calls
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Counting on a firewall or rate-limit rule on `/v1/` to limit the connector after switching to internal calls (`D-INTERNAL-ACCOUNT-TRUST`).
known_misuse.instead: internal calls do not pass the edge; limit who can deploy Workers instead

known_misuse.pattern: keep_approval mapped to an action the profile also gives where the approval should not stand, or from a rule that does not require what the approving rule requires
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Mapping `keep_approval` to an action that the profile also gives where the approval should not stand (a merged pull request, a later rule), or by a rule that does not require everything the approving rule requires, so a failed check on the same commit keeps the approval (`R-CONNECTOR-APPROVE`).
known_misuse.instead: an action of its own for the already-approved rule, after every blocking rule

known_misuse.pattern: an approving decision that changes because of the connector's own approval, without keep_approval: it approves and withdraws in turn on the runs other events start
known_misuse.why_unsafe: A profile whose approving decision depends on the connector's own approval without a `keep_approval` rule, so the connector approves and withdraws in turn on every run that another event starts (a finished check suite, a push, a person's review; since pointsman#216, `v0.15.0`, its own review events start no run, except as `D-CONNECTOR-OWN-REVIEW-EVENTS` says).
known_misuse.instead: github_app_approval with a keep_approval rule

known_misuse.pattern: renaming a profile's coderabbit_budget, coderabbit_queue or coderabbit_spend fact while its earlier decisions are still in the window: taken_by_other_pr, the queue's history and the spend are read by fact name and start from nothing
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Renaming a profile's `coderabbit_budget`, `coderabbit_queue` or `coderabbit_spend` fact while its earlier decisions are still in the window the facts read: the budget readings are still found by their fields, but `taken_by_other_pr`, the queue's history and the spend are read by the fact's name and start from nothing, so the queue and the spend count too little until the window has passed (`D-LOG-FACTS-NOT-ATOMIC`; docs/modules.md "Facts from the decision log").
known_misuse.instead: keep the fact names, or rename only once the window has passed

known_misuse.pattern: github_app_approval without bot_id
known_misuse.why_unsafe: A `github_app_approval` fact without `bot_id` (`R-APP-APPROVAL-BOT`).
known_misuse.instead: set bot_id

known_misuse.pattern: approving a workflow change because every github_workflows count is zero
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Approving a workflow change because every `github_workflows` count is zero, or skipping a person for `privileged` changes (`R-WORKFLOWS-TO-PERSON`).
known_misuse.instead: send privileged changes to a person

known_misuse.pattern: approving on github_release.version_only alone, or files that run in version_text_files
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Approving a release on `github_release.version_only` alone, or listing files that run in `version_text_files` (`R-RELEASE-PAIR`).
known_misuse.instead: pair with github_pr; exact files

known_misuse.pattern: treating coderabbit_spend as a hard cap with concurrent decisions
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Treating `coderabbit_spend` as a hard spending cap when decisions of the profile can be made at the same moment (`D-LOG-FACTS-NOT-ATOMIC`).
known_misuse.instead: set the hard limit at CodeRabbit

known_misuse.pattern: showing github_workflows.detail or a CodeRabbit fact's author as Markdown or HTML without escaping
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Showing `github_workflows.detail`, the CodeRabbit facts' `author` or any fact value as Markdown or HTML without escaping (§1.8).
known_misuse.instead: escape fact values for the grammar they go into

known_misuse.pattern: using the connector with AI questions on a public repository while counting on the author not seeing the answers
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Using the connector with AI questions on a public repository while counting on the author not seeing how the model answered (`R-CONNECTOR-PUBLIC-DECISIONS`).
known_misuse.instead: accept it or do not ask that profile there

known_misuse.pattern: switching answers on where not every writer may approve, or without the most-recent-push rule
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Switching answers in the pull request on in a repository where not everyone with write access may approve the pull requests in question, or without the ruleset's "most recent reviewable push" rule (`R-CONNECTOR-ANSWERS`).
known_misuse.instead: follow R-CONNECTOR-ANSWERS

known_misuse.pattern: asking a profile through the connector without people_answers
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Asking a profile through the connector without `people_answers`, so any action of the profile (and `reject`) can be given as the answer (`R-CONNECTOR-ANSWERS`).
known_misuse.instead: list people_answers

known_misuse.pattern: giving another client's token or a bound Worker the connector's profiles while counting on the connector's checks of who answers
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Giving another client's token, or a bound Worker, the connector's profiles while counting on the connector's checks of who answers (`D-RESOLVE-BY-SCOPE`).
known_misuse.instead: only clients that may answer its questions get those profiles

known_misuse.pattern: reading answered by or resolved_by as more than the connector's check at answer time
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Reading "answered by <login>" or `resolved_by` as more than the connector's check at answer time (`D-CONNECTOR-ANSWER-WINDOW`, `D-REVIEWER-IDENTITY`).
known_misuse.instead: treat it as the connector's claim, checked once

known_misuse.pattern: counting on answers in the pull request always being possible
known_misuse.why_unsafe: Counting on answers in the pull request always being possible, for example as the only way to unblock a release (`D-CONNECTOR-ANSWER-CAPS`).
known_misuse.instead: keep the review queue as the fallback

known_non_findings.reported_as: API tokens are hashed with plain SHA-256 instead of a slow password hash
known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers engine-api, config-repo; symptom 'credential-storage-weakness'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): the report concerns `TOKENS` records written by `scripts/tokens.mjs`; the token in question is a `pm_` token of 32 random bytes.
known_non_findings.suppression: TOKENS records written by scripts/tokens.mjs; the token is a pm_ token of 32 random bytes

known_non_findings.reported_as: a revoked token still works for up to a minute
known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers engine-api, engine-mcp; symptom 'stale-authentication'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): the token was revoked through `scripts/tokens.mjs revoke` less than about 60 seconds before the accepted request.
known_non_findings.suppression: revoked through scripts/tokens.mjs revoke less than about 60 seconds before the accepted request

known_non_findings.reported_as: a person removed from the GitHub organization can still use MCP
known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers engine-mcp; symptom 'stale-authorization'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): the grant was issued while the person was an active member; less than 7 days have passed; no new login happened.
known_non_findings.suppression: grant issued while an active member; less than 7 days passed; no new login

known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers engine-callbacks; symptom 'duplicate-delivery'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): the receiver did not answer 2xx within 10 s on the first attempt, or its 2xx was lost; the payloads are identical.
known_non_findings.suppression: no 2xx within 10 s on the first attempt or the 2xx was lost; identical payloads

known_non_findings.reported_as: the full state is visible in the AI Gateway logs although the decision log stores only a hash
known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers engine-api, engine-mcp; symptom 'information-disclosure'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): the deployment sets `AI_GATEWAY_ID` and the gateway has `collect_logs: true`.

known_non_findings.reported_as: untrusted issue text flows from the event payload to GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY or GITHUB_OUTPUT
known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers action-triage; symptom 'taint-flow-to-sink'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): the flagged values are the answers, probabilities, labels or decision id; the issue title and body are not among them.
known_non_findings.suppression: the flagged values are answers, probabilities, labels or the decision id; the issue title and body are not among them

known_non_findings.reported_as: text in the state made the model answer X and the policy acted on that well-formed answer
known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers engine-api, engine-mcp, bridge, action-triage, action-deploy-watch; symptom 'prompt-injection-steered-answer'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): every answer is inside the profile's types and options; the action is the one the policy produces for those answers; no answer outside the set and no action outside the profile's set (either would be `VALID` against `P-ANSWER-SHAPE` or `P-ACTION-FROM-POLICY`).
known_non_findings.suppression: every answer inside the profile's types and options; the action is the one the policy produces for those answers; no answer outside the set and no action outside the profile's set

known_non_findings.reported_as: InternalEngine.decide takes no token, so anyone can decide without one
known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers engine-api, connector-github; symptom 'missing-authentication'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): the call came through a service binding from a Worker in the engine's own Cloudflare account; it ran as the `INTERNAL_CLIENT` client with that client's profiles; no route or URL of the engine Worker reached the entrypoint (a URL that does would be `VALID` against `P-INTERNAL-CLIENT-FROM-ENGINE`).
known_non_findings.suppression: the call came through a service binding from a Worker in the engine's own account; it ran as the INTERNAL_CLIENT client with its profiles; no route or URL reached the entrypoint

known_non_findings.reported_as: a token holder can make the engine POST to any public https URL
known_non_findings.why_safe: Covers engine-callbacks; symptom 'ssrf-to-public-host'. Exact-match conditions (§1.15): the URL is public and https; the payload is the signed final answer; no private or loopback address was reached and no redirect was followed (either would be `VALID` against `P-OUTBOUND-PUBLIC-ONLY`).
known_non_findings.suppression: the URL is public and https; the payload is the signed final answer; no private or loopback address reached and no redirect followed
